screens.headline: Calibrate your display live
instructions: Open your monitor or TV picture menu while EyeCal is running. Start in Standard, Cinema, or Filmmaker mode and disable eye comfort, dynamic contrast, and automatic brightness.
For SDR, turn off Use HDR and auto colour management in Windows. For HDR, enable Use HDR and open an HDR test from All tests.
screens.should_see: Work through SDR in order or jump straight to a colour or HDR test.
screens.bad_example: A meter is needed for measured colour accuracy.
screens.name: Start here

screens.headline: Check the RGB range
instructions: Match RGB output range in your GPU control panel to HDMI Black Level or RGB Range on the display. Full pairs with Full and Limited with Limited.
Black looks grey: check for Limited output into Full input. Crushed shadows and clipped whites: check for Full output into Limited input.
screens.should_see: You should see steps in both rows, although the first dark steps can be subtle.
screens.bad_example: Bad example: dark and bright steps are crushed.
screens.name: RGB range

screens.headline: Adjust brightness for shadow detail
instructions: Adjust display Brightness or Black Level, not Backlight or OLED Pixel Brightness. Raise it until the first few strips appear, then lower it if the black surround turns grey.
Full-range RGB starts at code 0. Compare the above-black strips against the code-0 surround.
screens.should_see: You should see some above-black strips while the background stays black.
screens.bad_example: Bad example: the darkest strips disappear.
screens.name: Black level

screens.headline: Lower contrast until the whites separate
instructions: Lower display Contrast or White Level until the brightest strips separate. Keep the highest white bright without merging the steps.
If Contrast cannot recover the steps, check the GPU and display RGB range match.
screens.should_see: You should see small steps all the way to the brightest white.
screens.bad_example: Bad example: several top steps have merged.
screens.name: White clipping

screens.headline: Match the fine pattern to the solid grey
instructions: Select a target below, then adjust the display Gamma or EOTF preset until each top checker and its bottom solid look equally bright from your normal seat.
If the preset has no useful effect, reset black level and white clipping first and disable dynamic contrast.
screens.should_see: You should see similar brightness in each top checker and the matching solid below.
screens.bad_example: Bad example: the solid patches are too light.

settings.label: Target
descriptions: sRGB: the standard target for typical computer content.
2.2: a simple target for general viewing.
BT.1886: for dark-room TVs. This approximation assumes ideal black.

screens.name: Gamma

screens.headline: Check clean edges and the whole border
instructions: Lower display Sharpness or Edge Enhancement until halos disappear. If the screen-edge marks are missing, disable Overscan or enable Just Scan, Screen Fit, or 1:1.
If lines look soft, select the display native resolution and verify that the GPU is not scaling the image.
screens.should_see: You should see crisp individual lines, one clean edge, four corners, and a mark on each screen edge.
screens.bad_example: Bad example: bright and dark halos hug the edge.
screens.name: Sharpness

screens.headline: Toggle dither on the same ramp
instructions: Click the button below or press D to alternate between Off and blue-noise dither on the same ramp.
If dither helps, check GPU output depth and whether your source or player offers dithering. If both views show bands, turn off dynamic contrast and compare another input.
screens.should_see: When dither helps, stripes become finer and the gradient looks more continuous.
screens.bad_example: Bad example: large stripes interrupt the transition.
screens.name: Dither on / off

screens.headline: Compare dither on and off
instructions: Drag the divider and try each algorithm. The left stays Off; the right uses the selected dither.
If only the dithered side improves, try a higher GPU output depth or software dithering in your playback pipeline.
screens.should_see: Left uses no dither. Fine texture on the right can make bands less visible.
screens.bad_example: Compare both sides at the same brightness along each vertical ramp.
screens.name: Dither split

screens.headline: Compare 8-bit and 10-bit output
instructions: Switch depth with B or the button. Compare under the same display settings. The actual swapchain depth and presentation mode appear at top right.
If exclusive 10-bit helps, use 10-bit in your GPU control panel and keep the same signal path. If it does not, check GPU output depth, bandwidth limits, and the cable.
screens.should_see: The ramp should show the same range in both passes.
screens.bad_example: Broad bands with no improvement are a clue only in granted Vulkan exclusive mode.
screens.question: Use the two observed passes to narrow down the cause.
screens.name: 8 / 10-bit probe

screens.headline: Check the shadows and midtones
instructions: Turn off shadow boost, dynamic contrast and automatic brightness while comparing. Use the moving ramp to look for flicker or moving grain.
Select a symptom below for a concrete next check.
screens.should_see: Look for steps, moving grain, or flicker and note which region shows it.
screens.bad_example: Look for coarse bands or moving texture that distracts from the gradient.
screens.question: Get a next step for the symptom you see.
result_hints: Try turning off shadow enhancement. Compare local dimming On and Off; on a projector also compare dynamic iris modes.
Confirm 10-bit GPU output if available, try a different input or cable, and compare a known clean source with enhancements off.
Disable motion interpolation and dynamic contrast, then compare a fixed refresh rate or a different display input.
screens.name: Shadow banding
Greyscale tint
screens.headline: Check for tint in neutral greys
instructions: Select a neutral colour-temperature preset such as Warm or D65. Disable eye comfort and ambient white balance.
If mid-grey or white is tinted, compare presets. Use RGB gain for bright greys or offset for dark greys only if your display exposes them.
screens.should_see: The same neutral hue should hold from dark grey to white.
screens.bad_example: Example: an uneven red bias in the greys.

screens.name: Colour saturation
screens.headline: Separate the colour saturation steps
instructions: Reset Color and Tint to their neutral values, disable vivid colour enhancement, and select Auto or Rec.709 gamut for SDR.
If highly saturated steps merge, lower Color/Saturation until they separate. Leave per-colour CMS controls for a measured calibration.
screens.should_see: Each row progresses from neutral grey to its own hue without merging the last steps.
screens.pattern_label: Rows: red / green / blue / cyan / magenta / yellow

screens.name: RGB channel clipping
screens.headline: Keep bright RGB steps separate
instructions: Lower Contrast if multiple rows clip. If just one clips after a white-balance adjustment, undo the change or reduce that channel RGB gain slightly.
Recheck white clipping and neutral grey after each change.
screens.should_see: Codes 224 through 255 should progress in each channel.

screens.name: Solid fields
screens.headline: Inspect the screen with solid fields
instructions: Choose black, grey, white, red, green, or blue. Move your pointer away and inspect from your usual seat.
If a shadow moves when local dimming is switched off, compare its settings. A fixed dot on one or more fields can be a panel pixel defect.
screens.should_see: Look for fixed bright or dark dots, tint patches, and uneven brightness.
screens.bad_example: A fixed patch across inputs is a display-side clue.

screens.name: HDR peak clipping
screens.headline: Check HDR highlight clipping
instructions: Use an HDR picture mode. Compare static tone mapping, HGiG, or the game tone-map mode if available; avoid changing modes during a pass.
If the top steps merge, compare tone-mapping modes or lower HDR Contrast if it restores separation. Use the last distinct target as a starting point for the source peak setting.
screens.should_see: Bright steps can roll off smoothly or merge depending on tone mapping.

screens.name: HDR near-black
screens.headline: Recover HDR shadow detail
instructions: Adjust HDR Black Level or Shadow Detail. Raise it until some patches separate. Lower it if the code-zero surround turns grey.
Disable dynamic contrast, then compare local dimming with the same picture mode and viewing position.
screens.should_see: Black should remain dark while some above-black patches are visible.

screens.name: HDR reference white
screens.headline: Set comfortable HDR paper white
instructions: Compare the patches at your usual viewing distance. Change the game or playback app Paper White, UI Brightness or Diffuse White setting.
If HDR white looks blue or yellow, compare the HDR colour-temperature presets before changing white balance.
screens.should_see: Diffuse white should look comfortable while the separately tested peak highlights still stand out.

screens.name: HDR window size
screens.headline: Compare HDR brightness by window size
instructions: Switch windows and watch the same 600 cd/m2 signal. Keep the display settings fixed between sizes.
If larger windows dim strongly, compare Peak Brightness or Energy Saving modes. If the change remains, calibrate with that limit in mind.
screens.should_see: Any brightness difference between windows comes from the path or display response, not a higher encoded patch value.
screens.pattern_label: HDR10 600 cd/m2 through 2%, 10% and 25% of the pattern area
